model_annotation: The graph displays the daily number of new COVID-19 cases and the number of new media reports over time. The horizontal axis represents dates ranging from July 1, 2022, to April 30, 2022, marked at irregular intervals. The vertical axis on the left side is labeled with values from 0 to 1,800,000, with increments of 200,000, representing the number of people. The vertical axis on the right side is labeled with values from 0 to 6,000, with increments of 1,000, representing the number of media reports. The graph features two lines: one in blue, representing the number of new COVID-19 cases, and another in light blue, representing the number of new media reports. The blue line fluctuates significantly over time, with the highest point reaching approximately 1,600,000 cases and the lowest point at around 200,000 cases. The light blue line also fluctuates, but to a lesser extent, with values ranging from around 1,000 to 5,000 reports. The graph does not display any specific grouping or stacking of the bars, and the bars are not sorted in any particular order. Notably, there are no highlighted or emphasized bars in the graph. Overall, the graph provides a visual representation of the daily number of new COVID-19 cases and media reports over time, allowing for a comparison of the two trends.
